steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been going since you finished the ChiroThin Protocol with us? Are you still keeping the weight off and feeling great, has a little started to creep back, or are you pretty much back to where you were before you started?

(This question has only three possible answers. Click the one you hear.)

steps.title: Kept It Off: Credit the Maintenance Work
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that is FANTASTIC, and I want you to really hear this: keeping the weight off tells me you’ve been working the maintenance strategy, and that puts you in a group most people never reach. The weight loss was the program; keeping it off. That part was YOU.

Do you remember where you started? The number on the scale that finally made you pick up the phone? (Let them enjoy this. They earned it twice.)

steps.title: Some Crept Back: The Short-Course Path
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I’m really glad you told me, and here’s the most important thing I’ll say on this call: a little creep-back almost never means the program didn’t work. It usually just means life pulled you away from the maintenance rhythm, and the plan is DESIGNED to be picked back up.

(Let them respond. Zero blame, zero disappointment in your voice, “life happened” is the whole frame.)

And by the way. A lot of my patients tell me they tried other things in between: the shots, the programs, the apps. How about you? (Soft fish. Ask it lightly. If they mention GLP medications or injections, use the “They mentioned trying GLP/injections” button below. There’s a whole conversation for that.)

Well {{contact_first_name}}, I’m really glad I caught you, because this is exactly the kind of thing we want to know about.

(Do not pitch anything here, no programs, no timelines, no promises. The file update questions come next, and whatever matters most to them will surface there.)

steps.title: Mostly or All Back: The Full-Round Path, Maintenance First
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, thank you for being honest with me, and please hear this before anything else: you did not fail, and your body is not broken. Here’s what I know for certain: the program worked on your body. You lost the weight. That’s proven. What didn’t happen was the maintenance piece, and that’s the part we’re going to get right this time.

(Let them respond fully. Zero blame. The maintenance drift is “life happened,” never “you didn’t follow it.”)

And by the way. A lot of my patients tell me they tried other things in between: the shots, the programs, the apps. How about you? (Soft fish. Ask it lightly. If they mention GLP medications or injections, use the “They mentioned trying GLP/injections” button below. There’s a whole conversation for that.)

Well {{contact_first_name}}, I’m really glad I caught you, because this is exactly the kind of thing we want to know about.

(Do not pitch anything here, no programs, no round-two framing, no promises. The file update questions come next, and whatever matters most to them will surface there.)

steps.title: They Tried GLPs In Between: The Boomerang Conversation
steps.content:
(This patient has now watched TWO approaches “fail” them. Their silent objection is “nothing keeps the weight off. Why bother?” Your job: absolve the switch, reframe both regains as one lesson, and position round two as the completion.)

{{contact_first_name}}, honestly. I completely understand why you tried it. The results those medications produce while you’re on them are real, and half the country was talking about them. You don’t owe anyone an apology for trying.

(Pause. This kills any sheepishness they’re carrying about having left. No smugness, ever.)

But can I share what I think you actually learned from the whole experience? The medication worked right up until it stopped, because it was doing the work FOR you, and it left the day it left. ChiroThin worked too, but it came with something the injections never had: a maintenance strategy, the part that teaches your body and your habits how to KEEP the result. That’s the piece that didn’t get its turn last time.

So no. Your body isn’t broken, and it’s not true that nothing works. You’ve now proven two things: ChiroThin takes the weight off your body, and nothing keeps it off without a maintenance strategy. Round two is where we put those two lessons together, and this time the maintenance piece is the headline, not the fine print.

(Do not pitch or schedule here. Continue into the file update, whatever matters most to them will surface in the questions.)

steps.title: Booked: Wrap Up Warm
steps.content:
Perfect, you’re all set for (day) at (time), {{contact_first_name}}.

Come in exactly as you are, no pre-visit dieting, no weigh-in anxiety, none of that. We’ll take a look together, size things exactly right for where you are today, and get you back onto the strategy that keeps it off for good.

We can’t wait to see you!

steps.title: The Review & Bridge to Emotion
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I've got this right. (Recap what they told you: how long it's been going on, how often, and how it's been affecting them.) Did I get that right?

And it sounds like what you'd really love is to get back to feeling the way you did when things were going well. Is that fair to say?

(About 95% say yes. That yes is the moment. Don't rush past it.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Uncover Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you did mention {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is the timing just not right, or is there something else on your mind that's holding you back from taking a look?

(Warm and easygoing, no pressure, and never restate the concern back at them. You're just trying to understand what's in the way. Then stop and let them answer.)

What are your thoughts about that?

steps.title: The Transition: Update the File
steps.content:
Now {{contact_first_name}}, while I have you on the phone, I’d like to ask you a few additional questions so we get your file completely up to date. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes before starting the questions.)

steps.title: The Twelve Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Ask these in order. Critical: write down every symptom or concern they mention. You’ll read it back on the next screen.)

You mentioned some of it’s come back. Can I ask about how much we’re talking, and when you started noticing it creeping up? Was it gradual, or did something change? A stressful season, an injury, a schedule shift?

Are the eating habits you built during the program still mostly in place, or has life pulled you back toward some of the old patterns?

How’s your energy been through the day, still strong, or have you noticed the afternoon crashes creeping back in? Needing coffee or a little sugar boost to get through the afternoon?

How have you been sleeping? Falling asleep okay, staying asleep, waking up rested?

Do you ever feel irritable, or do you feel that you’re under a lot of stress?

Do you find yourself suffering with allergy or sinus problems, even if you think it’s normal?

Now that you’re carrying less weight than when you started, or even if some has come back, how has your body been feeling overall? Any aches or pains that have shown up or changed?

Are you experiencing any pain, stiffness, or soreness in the neck, mid-back, or low back, even if it’s mild, lasts less than five minutes, and goes away on its own?

What about your knees, hips, or feet? Anything that complains on stairs, first thing in the morning, or after you’ve been on them a while?

Is there anything you’ve cut back on? Walking, the gym, playing with the kids or grandkids, because something starts hurting when you push it?

Have you been experiencing any headaches, even if they’re mild, last less than five minutes, and go away on their own?

And finally, are you taking any medications, either prescribed or over the counter, even if it’s only once or twice a week?

(If they mentioned anything at all, use the notes you took during the questions and ask:)

Now {{contact_first_name}}, you just told me about (read back the issues they mentioned, e.g. “your sleep’s been rough and your back’s been bothering you”). What I’d like to know is: which one of these bothers you the most? In other words, if you could get rid of one of these and never have it bother you again, which one would you like it to be?

(If they genuinely mentioned nothing new, skip this question and pick the path below that fits.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, what I’d like to do now is ask you a few quick questions about {{main_concern}}, so I can get your file fully updated. It’ll only take a minute.

(Take the concern they named and make it real with three questions, in order. Write down or make note of their answers. You will use them in the next section. After each question, pause and let them fully answer. React like a human: “I see,” “Wow,” “That’s a lot.”)

How long has that been going on? A few weeks, a couple months, since you finished the program, or longer than that?

(Let them answer, then:) “[Repeat their answer back]? Would you agree with me that dealing with something like that for that long really isn’t OK?”

(If they shrug it off, “oh, I just deal with it”:) “You worked hard for those results. Watching them slip away for that long isn’t something you should just have to accept.”

And is it something you notice once in a while, or is it on your mind pretty much every day at this point, getting dressed, seeing photos, stepping on the scale?

(Let them answer, then:) “That’s a lot. And honestly, carrying that around every day isn’t just not OK. It’s not something you have to live with. Wouldn’t you agree?”

And the last thing I’d like to ask is how it’s impacting you. But first, do me a favor: think of a day when you felt great. You were at the weight you wanted, full of energy, everything clicking. Now think of the day you’ve felt the most frustrated with it. Do you have those two days in your head?

(Wait for the yes. Then walk that frustrating day through three areas, pausing after each:)

“On that day, what about work? Were you as productive as usual, as enjoyable to be around?” (Let them respond. “I see.”)

“What about at home? Were you fully engaged with the people around you, or did you kind of want to be left alone?” (Let them respond. “That’s really not OK.”)

“And the things you enjoy. Your hobbies, getting together with friends, family things. What happens to those on days like that?” (Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Then respond with empathy: Thank you for sharing that with me. It makes complete sense, and that’s exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}} help people with every single day.

steps.title: The Magic Question & Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it sounds to me like {{main_concern}} isn’t just affecting you. It may also be affecting the people you care about, keeping you from the things you enjoy doing, maybe even getting in the way at work. Do you see how that could actually be the case?

(Wait for their answer. If they say no or hesitate: “That’s completely fair, and honestly, I’m glad it hasn’t spilled over into the rest of your life. But it’s still been bothering you, and that’s reason enough.” Then continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you set up with an appointment so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look at you and see if there’s something {{rec_pronoun}} can do to help you with {{main_concern}}. If {{rec_pronoun}} can help you, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know, and {{rec_pronoun}}’d be honored if you let {{rec_obj}}. And if {{rec_pronoun}} don’t think {{rec_pronoun}} can help, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know that as well, because {{rec_pronoun}}’re not here to waste anybody’s time or money. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: The Weight-Focus Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, can I say something? You’ve already done the hardest part. You proved you can lose the weight, because you did it. What’s happening now isn’t a failure, it’s just drift, and drift is a lot easier to fix than starting from zero. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you set up with an appointment so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look at where things are and help you get back to where you were. If {{rec_pronoun}} can help you, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know, and {{rec_pronoun}}’d be honored if you let {{rec_obj}}. And if {{rec_pronoun}} don’t think {{rec_pronoun}} can help, {{rec_pronoun}}’ll let you know that as well, because {{rec_pronoun}}’re not here to waste anybody’s time or money. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Kept It Off: The Recalibration Close
steps.content:
Well {{contact_first_name}}, that’s actually part of why I’m calling. The maintenance strategy works best with an occasional recalibration. A quick check-in where we look at where you are, make sure the guidelines still fit your life, and tune anything that needs tuning. Think of it as protecting the win.

Let’s get you on the schedule. {{rec_pronoun_cap}} have time this week on (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: I should be able to do it myself this time
steps.content:
I completely understand, and that's a great mindset. A lot of people feel that way, and what coming back in does is simply give you the support and structure that made it work the first time, which is exactly what {{rec_pronoun}} can map out with you.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I’m embarrassed I gained it back
steps.content:
Please don't be. There's no judgment here at all. Life has a way of throwing curveballs at even the best routines, and the important thing is you already know the protocol works for you. You did it once; your body's proven it can do it. {{rec_pronoun_cap}}'d simply love to help you get back to where you were.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Cost (Weight Is Their Focus)
steps.content:
(Acknowledge it, then reframe around what the result was worth to them. You are scheduling an evaluation, not asking them to commit to anything today.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I completely understand. I want to be clear. This first step is simply an appointment so {{rec_pronoun}} can take a look. You’re not committing to anything. Can I ask? How much does getting back there matter to you? The way you felt in your clothes, the confidence when you saw yourself in photos, the compliments, the energy, feeling good in your own skin again. That version of you?

(Pause and let them answer. This is the question that does the work.)

And here’s something a lot of people don’t realize: depending on where things stand, you may not need the full protocol again. If only some of the weight has come back, the doctor can often size you into a much shorter course, and a shorter course means a much smaller investment than the first time around. That’s exactly what the appointment figures out.

(Do NOT improvise pricing, packages, or discounts on the call. Let the office handle specifics.)

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I thought that was behind me
steps.content:
I completely understand, and that's a great thing to bring up. These things can creep back over time with everyday wear and tear. It doesn't mean anything went wrong. And that's exactly the kind of thing {{rec_pronoun}}'ll want to look at with you in person.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I've seen a chiropractor: it didn't help
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad you told me. No two offices approach this the same way. A lot of it comes down to finding what's actually driving the problem in the first place, and that's exactly what the evaluation is for.

And I want to be clear. If we can help you with {{main_concern}}, we'll let you know and be honored if you let us. And if this isn't something we can help with, we'll tell you that too. We're not here to waste anybody's time or money.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: I need to think about it
steps.content:
That's completely fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's the right fit, which one is closest for you?

(Listen, their answer usually points to one of the other buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

Honestly, coming in is really just information. We take a look at where you're at with {{main_concern}}, you find out exactly what your options are, and then you get to decide with real answers instead of wondering. And if it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too.

Confirm and continue: Does that make sense? (Wait for a fast yes.) Do you have any other questions or concerns?

steps.title: Objection: Just send me information
steps.content:
I'd be glad to get you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a link or a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't look at where you're actually at and what would work best for you. That's really what the visit is for: we take a look and you get answers that apply to you, not just general information. So let me get you on the schedule first, and you'll have real answers to go on.
